# Staged test cases — candidate v0.7 (protocol revision 2026-07-28)

> **These fixtures are DRAFTED, NOT SCORED.** They are deliberately outside `../testcases/` so the
> reviewed v0.3–v0.6 corpus and every published number stay frozen while *"Measuring the Defenders"*
> is under review at AISec 2026 (decision 2026-09-03). No runner, scorer, or leaderboard reads this
> directory. `rubric/crosswalk.json` has no entries for these vector ids yet.

**Generated by** [`../scripts/gen-staging.mjs`](../scripts/gen-staging.mjs) — that file is authoritative.
Edit the generator, not the JSON. **Every claim** these fixtures encode is verified against
specification text in [`../docs/SPEC-VERIFICATION-2026-07-28.md`](../docs/SPEC-VERIFICATION-2026-07-28.md);
where verification contradicted a secondary source, the fixture follows the spec and says so in
`provenance`.

## Why these exist

On 2026-07-28 MCP shipped a breaking revision: the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions
were removed, server-initiated requests were replaced by MRTR, routing metadata was mirrored into HTTP
headers, list results became cacheable, Tasks became an official extension, and Roots / Sampling /
Logging / DCR were deprecated. Every existing MCP security benchmark — MSB, MCPTox, MCPSecBench,
AgentDefense-Bench, and this corpus — was authored against the older shape. These eight candidate
vectors model the surface the revision introduced.

## The candidates

| Vector id | Cases | Severity | Tests | Confidence |
|---|--:|---|---|---|
| `header-body-desync` | 3 | high | Mirrored routing headers disagreeing with the JSON-RPC body; Base64-sentinel evasion; an intermediary trusting headers under an unvalidated protocol version | **high** — normative, with error code `-32020` |
| `requeststate-forgery` | 3 | high / medium | Unprotected `requestState` tampering; cross-principal + expired replay; (secondary) tool state-handle hygiene | **high** for the MUSTs; the handle case is guidance-only |
| `list-cache-poisoning` | 3 | high | Implausible `ttlMs`; `cacheScope: public` on an authenticated authorization-varying list; **stale cache suppressing rug-pull detection** | **high** — spec-acknowledged |
| `mrtr-input-phishing` | 2 | high | Credential elicitation and injected `systemPrompt` sampling carried inside `input_required` | **high** |
| `task-authz-bypass` | 2 | high | Guessable task IDs and missing per-request authorization; `Mcp-Name` ≠ `params.taskId` on task methods | **high** |
| `mcp-app-sandbox-bypass` | 1 | medium | Whether a host actually enforces SEP-1865's iframe sandbox and egress-blocking CSP | medium — vendor framing corrected against SEP-1865 |
| `roots-scope-gap` | 1 | medium | Whether any filesystem boundary is enforced now that Roots is deprecated | medium |
| `transport-downgrade` | 1 | medium | Legacy session ID / GET stream / `Last-Event-ID` still honoured | medium |

**16 cases across 8 vectors.** Each has a malicious fixture, a near-identical benign control, the
expected defender behavior, and a `rationale` quoting the rule it derives from.

## Two of these changed under verification

Recording it here so the corrections are not lost:

- **`requeststate-forgery` was split.** Protocol-level `requestState` carries genuine **MUST**s (integrity
  via HMAC/AEAD; reject state that fails verification). Tool *state handles* are covered only by a section
  the spec marks **non-normative**. Conflating them would have overstated the finding, so the handle case
  is a separate, lower-severity fixture with `enforce: false`.
- **`task-authz-bypass` lost its enumeration variant.** There is no `tasks/list` in this revision — it was
  removed deliberately, and the spec cites that removal as a security improvement. What remains is a
  conformance test of ID entropy and per-request authorization.

## Extra fields on staged fixtures

Staged documents carry two fields the scored corpus does not:

- `"status": "staged-unscored"` — a machine-readable guard so nothing picks these up by accident.
- `"appliesTo": ["2026-07-28"]` — the protocol-revision axis. The same axis now exists as non-scoring
  metadata on every scored vector in `rubric/crosswalk.json`, because a coverage number is only
  meaningful relative to a protocol revision.

## Promotion checklist (do not start before 2026-09-03)

1. Add each vector to `rubric/crosswalk.json` with its full crosswalk row (layer, STRIDE, NIST AI RMF,
   OWASP LLM 2025, OWASP Agentic 2026, NSA) **and** `appliesTo: ["2026-07-28"]`.
2. Fold the entries from `gen-staging.mjs` into `scripts/gen-testcases.mjs` and regenerate.
3. Re-run every adapter. Re-measure. Publish the delta **per protocol revision**, not as one number.
4. Re-verify any fixture still labelled medium confidence against spec text before it reaches a paper.
